qt: to the Commission Georgios Kyrtsos (Renew) Subject:

According to a recent report by Transparency International, of the EU’s 27 Member States, Greece is the country that has seen the sharpest decline in the rule of law. The decline in matters pertaining to the rule of law, such as the restriction of press freedom, is leading to an increase in corruption in Greece. Transparency International ranks Greece among the top four most corrupt countries in the EU. As the European Centre for Press and Media Freedom has stated, the investigative newspaper Documento was initially targeted in statements issued by the Greek government and is now being targeted by the tax authorities. The Greek tax authorities imposed a crippling tax penalty on the newspaper for no legitimate reason. The fine undermines the economic viability of the newspaper and aims to restrict press freedom even further. According to Reporters Without Borders, when it comes to press freedom in the EU, Greece has been bottom of the pile for two consecutive years. In view of this, how is the Commission thinking of responding to the unfair taxation imposed on Documento and the Greek government’s persistence in restricting press freedom, despite the concerns raised by the Commission itself regarding the deterioration of the rule of law in Greece?
at: (English version) to the Commission Georgios Kyrtsos (Renew) (31 January 2024) Subject: The unfair taxation imposed on Documento newspaper and the restriction of press freedom in Greece According to a recent report by Transparency International, of the EU’s 27 Member States, Greece is the country that has seen the sharpest decline in the rule of law. The decline in matters pertaining to the rule of law, such as the restriction of press freedom, is leading to an increase in corruption in Greece. Transparency International ranks Greece among the top four most corrupt countries in the EU. As the European Centre for Press and Media Freedom has stated, the investigative newspaper Documento was initially targeted in statements issued by the Greek Government and is now being targeted by the tax authorities. The Greek tax authorities imposed a crippling tax penalty on the newspaper for no legitimate reason. The fine undermines the economic viability of the newspaper and aims to restrict press freedom even further. According to Reporters Without Borders, when it comes to press freedom in the EU, Greece has been bottom of the pile for two consecutive years. In view of this, how is the Commission thinking of responding to the unfair taxation imposed on Documento and the Greek government’s persistence in restricting press freedom, despite the concerns raised by the Commission itself regarding the deterioration of the rule of law in Greece? (26 March 2024) Media freedom and pluralism are a priority for the Commission. Member States should ensure an enabling environment for media and journalists operating in their territory. The Commission regularly monitors media freedom and pluralism in the Member States. Regarding Greece, the Commission refers to the 2023 Rule of Law Report (1). The challenges identified by the previous Rule of Law Reports have provided inspiration for several recent EU initiatives, including the proposed European Media Freedom Act (2), on which a political agreement was reached on 15 December 2023, and which contains, among others, safeguards against political interference in editorial decisions and against surveillance. The Media Freedom Act also requires that legislative, regulatory or administrative measures taken by a Member State that are liable to affect media pluralism or the editorial independence of media service providers operating in the internal market shall be duly justified and proportionate. Such measures shall be reasoned, transparent, objective and non-discriminatory. The Media Freedom Act is expected to improve the situation of media freedom in Greece and across the whole European Union. The Commission will continue to monitor media freedom and the framework for journalists’ protection in the Member States, including Greece, in the context of the 2024 Rule of Law report.

https://commission.europa.eu/publications/2023-rule-law-report-communication-and-country-chapters_en. The report includes a recommendation to Greece to take forward the process of adopting non-legislative safeguards and start the legislative process in relation to the protection of journalists, building on the activities initiated by the Task Force, in particular as regards abusive lawsuits against journalists and their safety, in line with the adopted Memorandum of Understanding and taking into account European standards on the protection of journalists. https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/IP_23_6635
